Collector's Card With A Picture Principle 2: Design a collector's card Principle 2: They used an innovative launch system designed by Rutan featuring a carrier aircraft and a suborbital rocket-powered space plane as a second stage (p. 23).

Collector's Card With A Picture Principle 3: Design a collector's card Principle 3: Overcoming a number of technical setbacks including a fatal crash, the company would lead the way in commercial spaceflight (p. 23).
Collector's Card With A Picture Principle 4: Design a collector's card Principle 4: Its test pilots earned the first commercial astronaut wings, award by the FAA in 2004 (p. 23).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Collector's Card With A Picture): Step 1 (Design a collector's card): Elon Musk (1971- ) formed Space Exploration Technologies (Space X) in 2002 to build rockets that could inexpensively carry payloads to low Earth orbit (p. 23).

Step 2 (Collector's Card With A Picture): Step 2 (Design a collector's card): After years of successful rocket launches, the company began transporting cargo to the International Space Station in October 2012 in its Dragon (p. 23).
Step 3 (Collector's Card With A Picture): Step 3 (Design a collector's card): For requirement 2, create a collector's card of your favorite space pioneer (p. 23).
Step 4 (Collector's Card With A Picture): Step 4 (Design a collector's card): Give details of the person's contribution to spaceflight, including dates, missions, and other accomplishments (p. 23).

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Many aerospace engineers are trained in mechanical engineering (p. 93).
Step 2 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Often they will specialize in areas such as structural design, propulsion systems, navigation and control instrumentation, and communications (p. 93).
Step 3 (Careers & Professional Pathways): A bachelor's degree in engineering is required for almost all entry-level engineering positions (p. 93).
Step 4 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Most engineers earn their degrees in electrical, electronics, mechanical, or civil engineering (p. 93).
